Both verification commands pass:

- `defects4j compile` → `compile` and `compile.tests` both **OK**
- `java -cp "$(defects4j export -p cp.test)" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormatAgentTest` → **OK (25 tests)**

## What was done

Created `src/test/org/apache/commons/lang/time/FastDateFormatAgentTest.java` — a single JUnit 3 test class (`extends TestCase`, `String`-name constructor, `suite()`/`main()`, `try/catch/fail` for error cases), matching the style of `DateFormatUtilsTest`, `StopWatchTest`, and `ValidateTest`.

### Coverage (public API only, 25 tests)

| Area | Tests |
|---|---|
| Style constants | `FULL/LONG/MEDIUM/SHORT` equal `java.text.DateFormat`'s and are distinct |
| Factories | `getInstance()` default pattern/locale/zone; pattern-only; forced `TimeZone`; `Locale` actually applied (German weekday vs English); instance caching returns same object with consistent `equals`/`hashCode` |
| Factory errors | `null` pattern → `IllegalArgumentException("The pattern must not be null")` (both overloads); invalid letter `"q"` → "Illegal pattern component"; invalid style `-1` for date/time/datetime instances |
| `format` outputs | `format(Date)`, `format(long)`, `format(long, StringBuffer)`, `format(Date, StringBuffer)` — exact strings against the "one billion seconds" instant in GMT; buffer identity + prefix preservation |
| Calendar zone semantics | unforced formatter uses the calendar's own zone (`GMT-5` → `20:46:40`); forced formatter overrides to `GMT` (`01:46:40`) **and does not mutate** the input calendar's hour/zone |
| `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)` | dispatch for `Date`/`Calendar`/`Long`; inherited `Format.format(Object)`; `String` → `"Unknown class: java.lang.String"`; `null` → message contains `<null>` |
| `parseObject` | returns `null`, resets `ParsePosition` index and errorIndex to 0 |
| `getMaxLengthEstimate` | exact values for `"yyyy"` (4) and `"yyyy-MM-dd"` (10); `>=` actual formatted length |
| Literals / quoting | `'Today is 'yyyy` → `"Today is 2005"` (est 13); `''` → `"'"` (est 1) |
| RFC822 / ISO8601 zones | `Z`/`ZZ` with `GMT` (`+0000`/`+00:00`) and `GMT-5` (`-0500`/`-05:00`) |
| SimpleDateFormat compatibility | 11 patterns (millis, era, text months/weekdays, escaped quotes, `zzzz`, day-of-year, etc.) formatted identically to a reference `SimpleDateFormat` on the same JVM |
| Style instances | `getDateInstance`/`getTimeInstance`/`getDateTimeInstance`: pattern equals the JDK's, exact `SHORT` output, structural checks for `FULL/LONG/MEDIUM`, cross-overload agreement, caching |
| `equals`/`hashCode` | reflexive; equal args; differing pattern/locale/forced-zone flag; `null`; non-`FastDateFormat` |
| `toString` | `"FastDateFormat[<pattern>]"` |
| Serialization | round-trip preserves `equals`, pattern, zone, locale, `maxLengthEstimate`, and produces identical formatted output (exercises the `readObject` → `init()` path) |

Locale-data-sensitive expectations are derived from `SimpleDateFormat` on the running JVM rather than hard-coded, so the tests are robust to CLDR differences (JDK 11 uses single-`y` locale patterns, which `FastDateFormat` renders as a 2-digit year — handled via `endsWith("05")` / reference comparison).
